adjudicated_statement: Work over C with Q-coefficients. Let X=M_{6,6}, let T=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(X;Q), identified with W_{26}H^{26}(X;Q)(21), and for a closed finite-type separated Deligne-Mumford substack Y' of X define K(Y'):=ker(T->W_{26}H^{26}(X\Y';Q)(21)). Assume the rational compactly supported cohomology of Y' agrees with that of its coarse moduli space, and use the Borel-Moore convention H^{BM}_k(Y';Q)=Hom_Q(H_c^k(Y';Q),Q). Poincare-Verdier localization identifies K(Y') with the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y';Q) in T. If dim(Y')<8, then H_c^{16}(Y';Q)=H^{BM}_{16}(Y';Q)=0 because 16>2dim(Y'), and therefore K(Y')=0. If Y' is contained in another closed support Y, factorization of open restriction gives K(Y') contained in K(Y). Consequently, a nonzero subspace of the ATT-0120 kernel T_Z supported on a closed Y' contained in its classifying-image closure Y requires dim(Y')>=8. The verified general ceiling is dim(Y)<=20; when the repaired PGL_2-quotient factorization of FND-0187 is included, dim(Y)<=17 and such supports can occur only in the range 8<=dim(Y')<=17. For a constant or product clause-(E) model Z_B=B times Z_0 whose classifying map factors through the fixed-fibre model Z_0 and whose classifying-image closure Y_0 has dim(Y_0)<=2, one has K(Y_0)=0 and K(Y_0) contained in T_Z. This conclusion concerns only target classes supported on Y_0; it asserts no compact-support pushforward from Z_B to T or T_Z, does not determine the Tate type of T_Z, and does not claim that such models are logically useless in proving the theorem.
contradiction_resolution: ATT-0121 section 4 correctly states the scheme-level vanishing H_c^k(W;Q)=0 for k>2dim(W), hence H_c^{16}(W;Q)=H^{BM}_{16}(W;Q)=0 when dim(W)<8. REV-0171 expressly confirms CLM-0121-3 and the kernel-form consequence. The stack extension is valid here with Q-coefficients through the coarse-space comparison for the relevant Deligne-Mumford quotient substacks. The localization interface of FND-0180 then gives K(Y')=im(W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y';Q)->T)=0. For arbitrary nested closed supports Y' subset Y, restriction to X\Y factors through restriction to X\Y', so K(Y') subset K(Y); the extra full-classifying-image hypothesis appearing in FND-0182 is unnecessary for this elementary monotonicity statement. ATT-0121 section 5 must not be used where it writes f_{B,!}:H_c^{16}(Z_B)->H_c^{16}(X): the nonproper classifying morphism supplies no such cohomological pushforward, exactly as REV-0171 objects. The valid conclusion is only support-side. The attempt's original derivation of dim(Y)<=17 by applying CLM-0112-8 directly over an etale atlas of Hbar^bal is outside that claim's verified scope; the ceiling 17 is retained only because FND-0187 separately repairs it via the PGL_2-quotient factorization. Absent that repair, FND-0181 supplies only dim(Y)<=20. Finally, the candidate's phrase 'inert in BOTH directions' is too broad: K(Y_0)=0 proves that constant/product models cannot supply a nonzero target class through this kernel-form support, but it does not establish that eliminating them cannot be useful supporting evidence, nor does it rule out a future independently constructed interface. Those overstatements are deleted rather than promoted.

hypotheses: Rational compactly supported cohomology of each relevant Deligne-Mumford quotient stack agrees with that of its coarse moduli space.
Borel-Moore homology uses H^{BM}_k(-;Q)=Hom_Q(H_c^k(-;Q),Q) in the same degree.
The identification of K(Y') with the image of W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Y';Q) in T is the localization and Poincare-Verdier interface recorded in FND-0180.
The sharper upper bound dim(Y)<=17 is used only with the repaired PGL_2-quotient factorization recorded in FND-0187; without that repair the verified bound is dim(Y)<=20 from FND-0181.
